passages.provision_quote: A. Each interscholastic or intramural athletic team or sport that is sponsored by a public school or a private school whose students or teams compete against a public school shall be expressly designated as one of the following based on the biological sex of the students who participate on the team or in the sport: 1. "Males", "men" or "boys". 2. "Females", "women" or "girls". 3. "Coed" or "mixed". B. Athletic teams or sports designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex. C. This section does not restrict the eligibility of any student to participate in any interscholastic or intramural athletic team or sport designated as being for "males", "men" or "boys" or designated as "coed" or "mixed".
passages.note: Enacted provision designates teams by biological sex and bars male-sex students from girls' teams while leaving other teams open to any student, matching rung 4 and excluding a total ban (rung 5).
Bolick voted Yea on the House Third Reading of this single-subject bill; the 31-24 margin is far from near-unanimous.
Bolick is listed as a House co-sponsor of this single-subject bill as filed.

rows.reasoning: As a State Representative, Bolick co-sponsored SB 1165 (2022) and voted Yea on its House Third Reading (BOLICK Y, Passed 31-24-5-0-0); the enacted bill designates school athletic teams by biological sex and bars students of the male sex from female-designated teams while leaving other teams open to any student, matching the rung requiring transgender athletes to compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth. This record is from her earlier House term in the same legislature and counts for her current Senate seat.
